title: Berry–Esseen bound with a quarter-power rate
statement: There is a constant $K>0$ such that the following holds. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent real random variables on a probability space, each with finite third absolute moment, with $\mathbb E X_i=0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb E[X_i^2]=1$. The Kolmogorov distance between the law of $\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$ and the standard Gaussian measure is at most $K\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb E|X_i|^3\bigr)^{1/4}$, with the same $K$ for every such family.
hypotheses_covered: A positive real constant K exists
A finite family indexed by Fin n
The random variables are mutually independent
Each random variable has finite third absolute moment
Each random variable has mean zero
The sum of the second moments equals one
